title: Abhishek Sharma Rises to No. 2 as Bumrah Cracks ICC T20I Top 10
excerpt: India's home series win over Afghanistan powered rankings gains across the board, with Varun Chakravarthy also climbing to fifth among T20I bowlers.
body:
• Abhishek Sharma rose one spot to No. 2 in the ICC men's T20I batting rankings, overtaking Pakistan's Sahibzada Farhan and closing to within 51 rating points of top-ranked Ishan Kishan.
  • Varun Chakravarthy climbed two places to No. 5 among T20I bowlers, while Jasprit Bumrah gained seven spots to break into the top 10 at No. 10.
  • The surge follows India's unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match home T20I series against Afghanistan in Delhi.
  • Arshdeep Singh (up 11 to 14th) and Axar Patel (up six to 27th) also climbed the bowling charts, and India lead England by one point in the T20I team standings.

India's dominant start to its home T20I series against Afghanistan translated into rankings rewards this week, with Abhishek Sharma climbing to No. 2 among the world's T20I batters and Jasprit Bumrah storming back into the top 10 among bowlers in the latest ICC update.

Context & Background

The defending T20 World Cup champions sealed an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series in Delhi, and several of their players made significant gains in the weekly rankings. Abhishek was one of the standout performers, his explosive 82-run knock in the opening match powering him past Pakistan opener Sahibzada Farhan, who slipped to No. 3 with 848 rating points.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=NZLyJwUF7k0

Abhishek's rise caps a productive series so far: he has amassed 121 runs from the first two games against Afghanistan, and his 862 rating points leave him 51 behind compatriot Ishan Kishan, who holds the top spot with 913. Two Indians now occupy the top two batting positions. England's Phil Salt is fourth, South Africa's Dewald Brevis fifth, and Jos Buttler moved up one place to seventh while India vice-captain Tilak Varma slipped to eighth.

There were other Indian movers as well. Sanju Samson climbed four places after his half-century in the second T20I, while Shreyas Iyer lost six spots to fall to 29th. Former captain Suryakumar Yadav, despite not playing international cricket for more than eight months, remains in the top 20.

Impact & Analysis

The bowling charts tell a similar story of Indian momentum. Varun Chakravarthy moved up two places to fifth after taking 1 for 16 in the series opener, though he has since been ruled out of the rest of the series and the Asian Games 2026. Bumrah, recently returned to action, gained seven spots to enter the top 10 with just two wickets to his name so far — a sign of how little separated the contenders behind the leaders.

The top of the bowling rankings remains spin-heavy: Afghanistan's Rashid Khan leads, followed by Pakistan's Abrar Ahmed, England's Adil Rashid and Australia's Adam Zampa. Arshdeep Singh's 11-place jump to 14th and Axar Patel's six-place rise to 27th underline how much of this update was driven by the Afghanistan series. In the all-rounder rankings, Afghanistan's Azmatullah Omarzai also made progress after his unbeaten half-century in the series opener.

The depth of the movement is the real story. With India holding a one-point lead over England in the T20I team rankings and Indians occupying two of the top eight batting slots and three of the top 14 bowling slots, the squad's home form is converting directly into global standing — useful capital ahead of their World Cup title defence.

Diaspora Angle

For diaspora fans, few sights are as satisfying as Indian players crowding the top of the ICC charts. The weekly rankings update is a standing ritual for the Indian cricket diaspora, and this one delivers: two Indians at one and two among batters, and Bumrah — the face of India's pace attack — back where his talent belongs.

What's Next

India will look to complete a 3-0 sweep in the final T20I, with fringe players pushing for permanent places. Beyond that, Chakravarthy's absence from the Asian Games 2026 squad will be felt, while Bumrah's return to the top 10 sets up an intriguing battle for the No. 1 bowler's slot as the World Cup title defence approaches.
